verdict.rationale: Skyfire auto-provisions a pre-funded wallet for each Buyer Agent. The agent spends from it via pay tokens that are committed against the wallet's available balance, and a wallet-balance API exposes available, held, pending-charge and pending-deposit amounts. User-side funding and control are thinly documented: the only documented funding flow is an Enterprise-only embed SDK, and controls are limited to account deactivation and per-token caps, with no per-token revocation. missing for 10: a documented self-serve way for an individual user to fund or top up the wallet, user-set agent spending limits or controls beyond token amount/expiry and account deactivation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can provision a wallet my agent holds and spends from — funded and controlled by me, with balance visibility

citations.quote: On signup, your Buyer Agent is created automatically, along with a pre-funded wallet so you can start using paid services right away.
At creation, the token's amount is committed against the buyer's wallet (which is why token creation requires the amount to be within the buyer's available balance)
Skyfire's Credits Wallet Embed SDK lets Skyfire Enterprise Customers embed wallet funding directly into their own application, through a secure, hosted flow.
New token creation stops at deactivation, but in-flight tokens are honored so sellers are paid for services they were legitimately asked to deliver.
